# #3608: Patch (part 4 of 6): loops that composite: every infinite animation moves only transform and opacity
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

Part of #3604. An animation on `box-shadow`, `filter`, `background-position`, `stroke-dashoffset`, `clip-path` or `text-shadow` makes the browser repaint the element every frame. One on `transform` and `opacity` runs on the compositor. 14 `infinite` animations in `apps/web/src` animate paint properties, several on many elements at once:

| Keyframes | File | Property | How many at once |
|---|---|---|---|
| `glow-breathe-ready`, `glow-breathe-condition` | `game/highlights.css` | box-shadow | every playable card in hand |
| `jk-facedown-breathe` | `game/facedown.css` | filter | every face-down card |
| `jk-veil-drift` | `game/facedown.css` | background-position | every face-down card |
| `cf-mythic-hand-shimmer` | `cards/cards.css` | box-shadow | every Mythic in hand |
| `end-turn-ready-pulse` | `game/board.css` | box-shadow | 1 |
| `clock-pill-pulse` (×2) | `game/clock.css` | box-shadow | 1 |
| `lane-pick-breathe` | `game/lanePick.css` | box-shadow | every lane offered |
| `duos-portal-flash` | `duos/duos.css` | box-shadow | 1 |
| `coach-pulse` | `tutorial/tutorial.css` | box-shadow | 1 |
| `skeleton-shimmer` | `skeleton/skeleton.css` | background-position | every skeleton |
| `drag-arrow-march`, `opponent-aim-run` | `game/drag/drag.css`, `game/aim/opponentAim.css` | stroke-dashoffset | 1 |

Rewrite each so the loop moves only `transform` and `opacity`. The usual way: the glow, shadow or tint drawn once on a pseudo-element, whose `opacity` (and `scale`) breathes. Each must look as close to today as the technique allows, and the static first layer the component spec reads (the 2px ring in `highlights.css`) stays as it is. Then add a guard so this doesn't come back. A test in the web's CSS suites (`fx/css.test.ts`, `motion.test.ts` or a new one) parses every stylesheet under `apps/web/src` and fails on an animation with `infinite` iteration whose keyframes set a paint property. Any loop that must stay goes in a named allow-list with its reason.

While there, check the 28 one-shot `filter` keyframes in `game/animations.css`. Move those that run on many elements together during combat (a board-wide hit, a sweep) to opacity over a pre-filtered layer where that is cheap and looks the same. Also check the 22 `will-change` declarations in `cards/cosmetics.css`: a `will-change` held on every face at rest costs a layer each. Keep one only while its animation runs.

### Acceptance

- None of the 14 loops above sets a paint property in its keyframes, and each still runs under the same conditions (existing tests and e2e selectors pass).
- The new CSS test fails on an `infinite` animation over `box-shadow`, `filter`, `background-position`, `stroke-dashoffset`, `clip-path` or `text-shadow` outside the allow-list (with a test proving it catches one).
- Reduced motion and `--anim-scale` behave as before.
- Screenshots of the hand glow, a face-down card and the end-turn button, before and after, in the pull request (`ui-walkthrough`).

Part of #3604
